source_contract.second_class_scope_rule: Accepted Chapter 5 propositions are outside subsections explicitly marked [一等].

review_basis: current official MLIT 第5版 Chapter 5 source/locators

decisions.rationale: 5.1.2 explicitly requires continuous in-flight monitoring of ownship condition and planned route/altitude/speed, weather changes, aircraft/other UAS, and third parties. This general operational monitoring set is distinct from existing no-assistant BVLOS telemetry requirements.
5.1.2 explicitly includes a preflight functional check of Remote ID when equipped. Existing Remote ID coverage tests exemption conditions, not normal-operation functional verification.

5.1.2 states that gasoline transported by passenger vehicle must use a Fire Service Act compliant dedicated container of 22 L or less. Existing engine questions do not test transport-container requirements.

5.1.2 specifically links engine-aircraft vibration to heightened checking for loose screws/fasteners. Q081 is a general preflight inspection proposition; this cause-specific engine inspection boundary remains distinct.

5.1.2 states that when no assistant is placed at the drop location, object-drop altitude is in principle within 1 m. Existing coverage addresses drop-device construction/procedure and legal definitions, not this operational height constraint.
5.1.3 explicitly requires Category II application submission by 10 business days before the planned flight start. Q082 tests the application-review-approval workflow, not this lead-time requirement.
5.1.4 explicitly distinguishes hull/camera damage insurance from liability insurance for operational third-party property/person damage. No canonical item tests this insurance-type mapping.
5.1.4 specifically requires checking whether transported cargo itself is within insurance coverage. This cargo-scope decision boundary is distinct from the general insurance-type distinction in C007.

5.1.4 explains software-tampering/commandeering risk and states that certified aircraft have cybersecurity conformity, making certified-aircraft use a mitigation. Q084 covers physical custody/security, not software-tampering mitigation.

5.2.1 explicitly requires capability to operate without GNSS position estimation in an emergency. Existing GNSS questions concern accuracy/waypoint effects; auto/manual takeover questions do not test GNSS-independent operation itself.

5.2.1 explicitly instructs elevator and aileron correction to stabilize horizontal position during GNSS-off hovering. This concrete control response is distinct from C010's general GNSS-independent capability.

5.2.1 requires helicopter takeoff/landing sites to be level, non-slippery, and to avoid sand/dry soil due downwash visibility risk. Existing helicopter/Risk coverage addresses area size, isolation, ground effect and wind, not this surface-condition proposition.
5.2.1 requires sufficient rotor speed before helicopter liftoff because low rotor speed can delay aircraft response. No canonical item tests this takeoff sequencing requirement.

5.2.1 requires not approaching a normally landed helicopter until the rotor stops. Q087 concerns accident-site immediate safety around a potentially powered/crashed aircraft, so the normal post-landing procedure is a distinct operational boundary.

5.2.1 requires a level fixed-wing runway without overgrown grass because slope can destabilize ground roll and grass can contact the propeller. No canonical item tests this runway-surface selection rule.

DRONE-Q-000130 already tests the same answer-defining proposition: fixed-wing takeoff/landing should select a headwind direction and tailwind creates stall risk. C016 changes wording/context but not the required reasoning boundary, so it is a semantic duplicate.

5.2.2 explicitly requires onsite preconfirmation of obstacles along an automatically configured waypoint route to mitigate setup-related collision/crash. Existing auto-flight questions test repeatability and GNSS route error, not this preflight human-error control.

5.2.2 identifies manual-control orientation/distance-perception errors and recommends all-direction control and specified-distance landing practice. Existing manual-control coverage tests use-case suitability or takeover, not this targeted training mitigation.

5.4.1 explicitly lists five CRM nontechnical skills for effective TEM: situational awareness, decision making, workload management, teamwork, and communication. Existing CRM/TEM items test the framework and stage management, not this skill set.

5.4.2 states that because the pilot must concentrate on aircraft movement/control, assistants principally handle flight preparation, route safety management and third-party access management. Q089 tests advance staffing/assignment/communication coordination, not this primary role division.
